limitations: Application-owned immutable metadata snapshot for the selected server. Application coordinates replacement and holds references across readers. No network, worker, new shared runtime, automatic refresh, credential handling or implicit business replay is introduced.

Only full OK/NONE publishes outputs. Complete supported extraction includes not_key routing arguments and overlapping specification occurrences. Unsupported/incomplete/future rules require authorized server assistance; unknown commands are distinct. Arity/index/count validation is not full business grammar validation. Variable access flags are possibilities and do not authorize replica reads.

Warm paths perform argument/span validation, hash lookup, bounded keyword scans, CRC over all selected routing key bytes and an optional second extraction pass. They have real CPU/scan/function costs even though requested heap is zero. Constructor retains Reply and allocates one index block; retained metadata/old snapshots/allocator overhead remain real storage.

Raw benchmark mode knows four key positions in advance and omits metadata/argument validation. It is an algorithm cost reference, not functionally equivalent client performance or zero-overhead evidence. Samples are unpinned serial closed-loop CPU batches; ns/op is an average, not P99. No upstream client/end-to-end/native Linux/mixed-load/CPU/RSS/72h acceptance.

Real Redis oracle uses owned plaintext WSL fixtures and offline native Windows/WSL C parsers. Business invocations are arguments to COMMAND GETKEYSANDFLAGS, never executed. SPUBLISH not_key is excluded by that server oracle; it uses the public standard position and actual server CLUSTER KEYSLOT, recorded separately. No C transport/TLS/Cluster failover claim.

Automatic metadata fetch/cache publication, server-assisted exotic command extraction, Cluster submission wiring, replicas/synchronous Cluster facade and full four-library completion remain open.
